transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-03 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Alex (Redwood CSM), Marta (Verdant Head of MLOps), Ian (Eng Manager), Samir (SRE), Leah (Product)

Summary (auto): quick demo of Redwood's Eval/Quality Monitoring. Walk through prompt set upload, running batch evals, setting regression alerts, and A/B comparisons. Discuss pilot logistics and security docs.

00:00 Jordan (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you carving out time today, we were planning about 45 minutes but put aside an hour in case we dig into benchmarks.
00:18 Marta (Verdant): Thanks, Jordan. Yep, quick note, we have a fairly tight timeline — execs want POC results in two weeks if possible.
00:27 Jordan: Understood, we'll cover what we can and outline the sandbox steps to get you running fast. Priya will lead the product walkthrough.
00:35 Priya (Redwood SE): Hi all. Quick agenda: show prompt set workflow, how to run batched evals via the Console and API, set up regression alerts, plus A/B comparison flows and how Optimize recommends quant/latency tradeoffs.
00:47 Ian (Verdant): Cool — we care about both quality regressions and cost tradeoffs, so that A/B comparison bit is key.
00:55 Priya: Great. Jumping in — on the Console home you can see Eval -> Projects. (screen share) Here I've uploaded a few prompt sets — you can import CSV or JSONL, or connect via S3.
01:20 Priya: The prompt set format we recommend is simple: prompt_id, input, expected_output (optional), and tags. For A/B you can tag variants.
01:35 Samir (Verdant): Quick Q: do you store the raw prompts in your hosted offering? Data retention and encryption?
01:45 Jordan: Short answer, yes we store eval artifacts but they can be configured — default retention is 90 days for hosted; Dedicated/Private allows custom retention and you can opt for customer-managed KMS. We'll send the security pack after.
02:02 Marta: We need SOC2 + SSO, and also on-prem evaluation possibility — some PII in prompts.
02:12 Jordan: We are SOC2 and ISO certified, and Private deployments support on-prem/audited pipelines. I'll attach the SOC2 cert.
02:25 Priya: Back to the Console — when you run an eval you can pick a baseline model version and a set of candidates. The console computes metrics per prompt and aggregate metrics: accuracy, rouge-like, BLEU-like, and custom NLI-based scoring if you provide reference outputs.
02:52 Priya: Here's an example run we did last week where we ran 5k prompts across two model variants and then used the regression alert wizard to create a rule — if aggregate metric drops by >3% or more than 100 prompts fail, trigger an alert.
03:15 Leah (Verdant): How noisy are the alerts? We don't want a flood every rollout.
03:24 Priya: You can tune thresholds and add noise filters — e.g., require X consecutive failing deploys, or require impact on high-value prompt tags only. Also, alerts can attach example prompts so SRE/ML teams can triage quickly.
03:40 Ian: Can we attach ownership tags so alerts route to a Slack channel or to PagerDuty?
03:47 Priya: Yep. Integrations: Slack, PagerDuty, Jira. You map tags to routing policies.
04:00 Priya: Now API side — the evals have a REST endpoint so you can POST a prompt set or reference S3 locations and kick off runs programmatically. We also provide a Python SDK snippet for automating nightly regression checks.
04:22 Priya: Example: from redwood import eval; eval.run(bucket='s3://verdant-eval', baseline='rwd-4b-v1', candidates=['rwd-4b-v2','rwd-3b-quant'], tags=['nlp-helpdesk']) — this runs async and returns a job id.
04:44 Samir: Does the job actually hit production endpoints or simulated ones? We don't want eval traffic to affect prod capacity.
04:52 Priya: Evals are routed to dedicated eval pools that don't impact customer production capacity. For Hosted customers we have separate capacity, for Dedicated you can reserve evaluation queues.
05:05 Jordan: Also worth noting we have prefix/KV caching exclusion flags so you can decide whether to use cached responses for evals or force cold runs.
05:18 Marta: Good — we want cold-run accuracy comparisons.
05:22 Priya: Great. Moving to A/B comparisons — you can run side-by-side scoring and the UI will surface per-prompt diffs and aggregate deltas with statistical significance indicators (t-tests / bootstrap approximations).
05:45 Priya: Here's a live A/B that compares model variant A (rwd-4b-v1) vs B (rwd-4b-q8) across our helpdesk prompt set. The UI shows per-tag breakdown, median latency, token cost delta, and quality delta.
06:05 Ian: Do you show per-token cost or per-inference cost?
06:11 Priya: Both. Cost is broken down: model compute tokens, tokenization overhead, and infra cost estimate. You can export cost projections for monthly run rates.
06:26 Leah: Can we plug in our own metric (like business KPI) rather than BLEU?
06:32 Priya: Yes — you can define custom metrics via a small lambda-style evaluator or upload a scoring script. We run it in a sandboxed runner. Note: for hosted we require script review for security; for Private you can run local evaluators.
06:50 Jordan: (interrupting) Quick note on regressions: the alerting ties to model rollouts so you can configure canary windows — e.g., deploy to 5% traffic, run eval on recent production prompts, if regression > threshold we auto-roll back or reduce to baseline.
07:12 Marta: The canary rollback is exactly what we need if a new quantized build regresses. How automated is rollback?
07:20 Priya: You can choose manual or automatic rollback. We typically recommend manual for first few runs. Automatic can be enabled for mature pipelines.
07:28 Samir: About quantized models — do you have guidance on q8 vs q4 in terms of quality delta?
07:34 Priya: Optimize will recommend quant/size tradeoffs based on your prompt distribution. We profile representative prompts and suggest quantization points where cost savings are high but quality regression minimal, and we surface expected token cost delta and latency improvements.
07:55 Ian: Do you do kernel-level profiling per hardware family?
08:01 Priya: Yes, the runtime picks kernels based on architecture and we have benchmarks per GPU family. For Dedicated we can pin to specific instance types.
08:10 Marta: Show us how an alert looks in detail.
08:14 Priya: (clicks) Alert detail includes failing prompt examples, delta chart over time, impacted tags, suspect model versions, and an action button to open a debug session which includes raw request/response and the KV cache state if relevant.
08:35 Ian: Can we redact PII before it shows up in the UI?
08:40 Priya: You can enable PII masking at ingestion, or opt to not persist raw inputs. For Private deployments you can choose to never ship raw prompts to Redwood control plane.
08:53 Marta: That helps. For the POC we will likely use masked inputs.
08:59 Jordan: Next I'll show the API snippet to pull failing examples and create a Jira ticket automatically.
09:05 Priya: Also worth noting we support snapshot diffs which are handy for compliance — you can snap eval baselines and archive them.
09:14 Leah: Can the evals be triggered from our CICD?
09:18 Priya: Yes — webhook or SDK invocation. Typical pattern: run unit tests, then run smoke evals against canary, then gate merge on no-regression.
09:32 Samir: Do you have a recommended sample size for statistical significance?
09:36 Priya: Typically 500-1k prompts for median-level confidence but depends on variance of your workload — we surface power analysis recommendations in the UI.
09:48 Ian: Let's talk infra: we currently run on GCP with a mix of T4s and A100s for heavy inference. Any blockers for dedicated pools?
09:58 Jordan: We can support GCP and AWS — Dedicated pools can be provisioned in your cloud account. If you need on-prem, there's a Private package. We'll coordinate infra specifics in the POC kickoff.
10:12 Marta: Timeline question — if we start the sandbox this week, can we have initial reports in 7-10 days?
10:18 Jordan: Yes, with prompt sets and access we'll run an initial benchmark and share a report within that timeframe.
10:24 Priya: Now I'll demo a sample night-run automation — opening the sandbox we've preloaded a small helpdesk prompt set (about 1.2k prompts). Running the job now so you can see results stream.
10:42 Priya: (job running) You'll notice progress updates and partial metric aggregates every minute. The transcript may show some minor stutter — sorry t-y typing — let me highlight the failing prompts bucket.
11:05 Priya: Here's a per-prompt diff view — see prompt 214 showed a hallucination increase on variant B, flagged by our NLI-based post-hoc comparator.
11:20 Marta: Can you export these failing prompts so our annotation team can triage?
11:25 Priya: Export CSV or push to S3; can also auto-create tickets with examples and metadata.
11:35 Ian: On A/B comparisons, is the significance calc conservative? We need to avoid false positives during noisy days.
11:42 Priya: We use bootstrap CIs by default with configurable alpha; also allow rolling-window smoothing.
11:52 Jordan: Real quick — competitors: we see customers comparing us to OpenAI for hosted simplicity and ModelServeCo for infra control, but our sell is evaluation tooling + rollouts + cost-optimize recommendations.
12:08 Marta: Noted. Any limits on prompt set size for hosted evals?
12:15 Priya: For hosted evals we support up to 100k prompts per job; we recommend chunking larger sets and running incremental analysis. For Dedicated/Private we can scale further.
12:28 Samir: Ok, question about tokens — do you compute embeddings for semantic similarity as part of the eval?
12:34 Priya: You can add embeddings as a metric; we run vector similarity checks and cluster failure modes. This is handy for identifying prompt clusters with regressions.
12:46 Leah: Walk me through how we'd run an A/B on our customer-facing summarization prompts. We want to measure both ROUGE and a business metric (resolution rate).
12:58 Priya: Upload prompt set with expected outputs if you have them, attach a custom scorer that maps model output to 'resolved' or 'not resolved', then run the A/B and in the UI select 'business KPI' view. We can also ingest telemetry to tie predictions to real-world resolution rates.
13:20 Ian: If we need to run heavy throughput tests, can we configure batching and autoscaling for the eval pool?
13:27 Priya: Yes — eval pools respect autoscale policies and batching config. You can cap concurrency to control cost.
13:36 Jordan: I'm going to pause for a sec to answer Marta's security follow-ups. Jordan: We'll send the SOC2, ISO docs, data flow diagram, and the SSO/SAML integration guide. If you'd like, Alex will coordinate an architecture review with our security team.
13:53 Alex (CSM): Happy to — we can schedule a security deep-dive next week.
14:01 Marta: That'd be helpful. Also, can you confirm export controls for EU data? We have EU customers.
14:09 Jordan: Yes, we support region pinning and data residency controls for EU region; we'll include those details.
14:20 Samir: A couple of nitty-gritty: do eval logs include token-level timestamps? We need them for latency root-cause.
14:29 Priya: We capture latency per request and per token-level breakdown where available; some runtime metrics vary by backend but we expose a detailed trace for Dedicated.
14:40 Ian: Ok great. Any gotchas with private deployments and the eval runner?
14:46 Priya: The main difference is that custom scoring scripts run locally in Private, while hosted requires script vetting. Also keys and KMS are customer-managed in Private.
14:58 Marta: For the POC, we want to run: (1) three prompt families (support, billing, onboarding), (2) baseline vs quantized and bigger model, (3) A/B with business-KPI scorer, (4) set regression alert for >2% drop in KPI.
15:20 Jordan: Sounds good. We'll provision a sandbox and a Dedicated eval pool for the POC to avoid impacting prod. Priya will run the first batch and we'll deliver an initial report.
15:34 Leah: Can you also add sample dashboard widgets we can embed into our internal reporting?
15:40 Priya: Yes — dashboards export as embeddable iframes or via the API. We'll share example snippets.
15:50 Ian: One more: what's the monitoring window for rolling canaries? We likely want 30-60 minutes.
15:56 Priya: Canary windows can be set from minutes to day-level; typical is 30-60 minutes for real-time rollouts.
16:06 Samir: Anything about cost estimates for nightly evals?
16:10 Priya: The Console shows projected monthly cost based on job size and compute choice; Optimize will give suggestions to reduce cost by batching or quantization.
16:22 Jordan: Ok we're at about 16 minutes into the call — I'll fast-forward a bit and show the final run results we already prepared from a similar customer.
16:34 Priya: (shows report) This report includes per-prompt failure heatmaps, the A/B delta table, and a suggested rollback decision tree.
17:05 Marta: Helpful. Can we see the raw job log for one failing example?
17:12 Priya: (clicks) raw request/response, tokenizer tokenization, matching score, and NLI comparator output. Note: some product names in the transcript may be mis-typed — e.g., Redwood Optimize sometimes appears as Redwood Optima in older logs.
17:34 Ian: Ha, noted.
17:40 Jordan: Let's cover pilot success criteria—Marta?
17:45 Marta: We need: 1) automated nightly evals running on three families, 2) A/B report showing delta and business KPI mapping, 3) regression alerting integrated with our Slack, and 4) a go/no-go recommendation delivered within 10 days.
18:05 Jordan: We'll commit to that.
18:10 Priya: Last piece — integration checklist: prompt set format, S3 access or CSV upload, VPN or VPC peering for Dedicated, SSO SAML metadata, and test account list.
18:26 Ian: I'll share our S3 bucket and IAM roles.
18:30 Samir: We'll also share expected traffic profile so you can provision the right eval pool.
18:35 Jordan: Great. Any final questions?
18:40 Leah: One small ask — can you show the A/B export format? We need to ingest it into our BI.
18:46 Priya: Export is JSONL with per-prompt metrics and aggregated summary; we'll attach a sample.
18:52 Marta: Sounds good.
18:56 Jordan: Quick recap of next steps — I'll send docs and pricing, Priya will stand up sandbox and run first eval, Marta/Ian to share prompt sets and infra details.
19:10 Jordan: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with calendar invites for the security deep-dive and POC kickoff.
19:18 Meeting end.

Note: transcript contains typical speech disfluencies and occasional mis-transcription of product names and acronyms (e.g., "Optima" vs "Optimize", "KV cache" sometimes transcribed as "K-V cash").
